summary: Plan sampling, interpret exposure results and prioritize controls for workplace hazards. Explore the occupational exposure assessment course.
lede: Occupational hygiene and workplace exposure risk assessment focuses on determining how workers may be exposed and what action findings warrant. It is for occupational health professionals, hygienists and safety managers who need to profile exposure groups, plan representative sampling, interpret results and prioritize controls for hazards such as dust, chemicals, noise, heat, vibration and biological agents. The course also covers communicating findings and tracking corrective actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who plan, interpret or act on workplace exposure information across industrial and occupational health settings.
prerequisites: Prior experience in occupational health, workplace safety, industrial operations or a related technical role is recommended. No coding is required. You should be familiar with workplace hazard identification; prior experience operating exposure-monitoring instruments is useful but not essential.
